stem: In a survey of 120 customers, 70 purchased product A and 55 purchased product B. If 25 purchased both products, how many customers purchased product A but not product B?

per_option_rationale.rationale: A but not B = n(A) - n(A intersect B) = 70 - 25 = 45.
This returns n(A) = 70, the count for A including those who also bought B, ignoring the need to exclude the overlap.
This comes from 70 + 25 = 95, incorrectly adding the intersection instead of subtracting it.
This comes from n(B) - n(A intersect B) = 55 - 25 = 30, computing B but not A instead of A but not B.

explanation: The number of customers who purchased A but not B is the part of the A-circle that lies outside the B-circle: n(A) - n(A intersect B) = 70 - 25 = 45.

explanation_sections.punchline: A but not B strips the overlap from A: subtract those who bought both from the A count.
explanation_sections.approach: State the formula: n(A \ B) = n(A) - n(A intersect B). Substitute directly.
explanation_sections.lesson: A only = n(A) minus the intersection. B only = n(B) minus the intersection. These are the exclusive regions.
explanation_sections.timing: 40 s. The trap is returning n(A) = 70 (forgetting to remove those who also bought B).
